reviews.summary: Read native/bunny-owned-process.c (260 lines) and the JS callers in src/lib/bunny-host/owned-process-group.server.ts. No resume-before-membership path, double close, or use-after-free was found on the enumerated launch failure paths. Reduced job access (ASSIGN|QUERY|TERMINATE) covers every call made: JOB_LIST, IsProcessInJob, TerminateJobObject, and the Query calls. HANDLE_LIST contains only stdio, and the stdin write end is non-inheritable. Findings: one MEDIUM contract mismatch (close drops the job handle even when ActiveProcesses is still above 0), one LOW diagnostic misreport, one LOW writer-thread cancellation race, one LOW main-thread blocking window, one latent LOW global-list thread-safety issue guarded by isMainThread, and one LOW GC-finalizer kill that leaves the JS record stale.

rows.title: close_group drops the job handle even when ActiveProcesses is still above 0
rows.reproduction: A member survives TerminateJobObject past the 1.5 s wait in terminate_group. close_owned (line 215) calls close_group, which runs CloseHandle(g->job) and sets g->job=NULL regardless of the returned active count. JS OwnedProcessGroup.close (owned-process-group.server.ts lines 165-166) then sets this.handle=null and record.closed=true. The Host can no longer inspect or re-terminate the group, and the session is recorded closed while ActiveProcesses is above 0. The contract says unconfirmed termination keeps the handle and the session counts as live code until the kernel reports 0.
rows.rootCause: close_group treats close as unconditional. KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE still kills stragglers on last-handle close, but that is asynchronous and unobservable to the Host. The explicit close path does not honor the keep-handle-while-unconfirmed rule that terminate_owned (line 218) follows.
rows.repair: In close_group, keep g->job open while active is nonzero (including the -1 query-failure value) and return without closing. Only drop the handle after ActiveProcesses reaches 0, or have close_owned refuse close and leave the record unconfirmed. Verify that liveCodeExecutions counts containment unconfirmed records as live.

votes.reasoning: The close_group defect is real in the C code: native/bunny-owned-process.c:76 runs CloseHandle(g->job) and sets g->job=NULL regardless of the active count returned by terminate_group, and close_owned (line 215) returns that count. The described failure does not occur on the reachable provider-session path. In src/lib/bunny-host/adapters.server.ts terminateJob (lines 301-308), the handle is closed only when active===0. Otherwise it records containment "unconfirmed", keeps the handle, and retries every 5 s (lines 307-315), which is the contract. The retry path (line 312) also closes only at 0. The only provider-path calls to OwnedProcessGroup.close with survivors present are the spawn-time inspect-failure catch (owned-process-group.server.ts:148) and the adapter's launch-failure catch (adapters.server.ts:335). Both are refusal paths with no live provider session, and the second is a no-op if close already ran. The release hook (owned-process-group.server.ts:147) routes to stop() when stopping is set, which the contained session always sets (adapters.server.ts:332). Probes (adapters.server.ts:87-89) use runWindowsOwnedProcess with no provider owner, so containment is undefined, and a probe timeout that drops the handle does not produce a live-code record. Even where the handle is dropped with survivors, the native launch sets JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and inspect enforces limitFlags 0x2000, so the last-handle close kills the stragglers in the kernel. The residual gap is observability and a deviation from the terminate_group "keeps the handle" comment, not a bypass. I did not run any tests or touch processes.

The native defect is real but narrower than claimed. native/bunny-owned-process.c:72-76 (close_group) runs CloseHandle(g->job) unconditionally after terminate_group, and the return value is only reported. The JS close at owned-process-group.server.ts:162-168 then sets handle=null and closed=true. Only the reported count, not the handle, is conditioned on active processes.

The claimed failure does not reach provider sessions. adapters.server.ts:298-306 calls owned.close only when owned.terminate() returns 0 after the bounded wait. Otherwise it annotates containment "unconfirmed" (line 307), keeps the session live, and retries via terminate (lines 310-315). close is called on retry only when now===0 (line 312). The stop path (line 368) goes through terminateJob too. So provider sessions keep the handle while unconfirmed, as the contract requires.

Residual reachable cases: (a) runWindowsOwnedProcess (owned-process-group.server.ts:199, probes) calls group.close(state) on root exit even with live descendants. These records carry no containment field, so nothing counts them as live. (b) Host shutdown through trackOwnedGroup's release callback (line 147) calls close("stopped") without a count check. In both cases the kernel still enforces the end: TerminateJobObject runs first (native line 67), and the last handle close triggers KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (native line 129). The job handle is the only one, since the reduced duplicate is held alone and HANDLE_LIST limits inheritance to stdio (native lines 132-133, 146). The gap is Host observability and bookkeeping (a closed record with containment "unconfirmed" still shows nonzero activeProcesses, and restart treats closed-unconfirmed as live via recoverProviderSessions line 102). It is not an escape. Severity LOW hygiene. Repair: have close_group return without closing while active is nonzero or -1, or make close() refuse when the count is nonzero.

rows.title: Membership-failure error is mislabeled when IsProcessInJob itself fails
rows.reproduction: If IsProcessInJob returns FALSE (API failure), member stays FALSE and the code sets error to ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED instead of the real GetLastError(). Fail-closed still holds because TerminateProcess runs. Only the diagnostic is wrong.
rows.rootCause: The ternary consults GetLastError() only when member is TRUE, which is the inverted condition.
rows.repair: Capture the IsProcessInJob return value separately. Use GetLastError() when the call returned FALSE, and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED only when the call succeeded with member FALSE.

votes.reasoning: Confirmed real but diagnostic-only. native/bunny-owned-process.c:152-153 reads `BOOL member=FALSE; if(!IsProcessInJob(pi.hProcess,job,&member)||!member){error=member?GetLastError():ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED;TerminateProcess(pi.hProcess,1);goto failed;}`. The `member?GetLastError():ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` ternary is inverted. The GetLastError() branch is only reachable when member is TRUE while the branch was entered, which requires IsProcessInJob to return FALSE after setting member TRUE. When IsProcessInJob fails, member stays FALSE, so the code always reports ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED and the real API error is lost. Fail-closed holds: the root is still suspended (CREATE_SUSPENDED, not yet resumed), TerminateProcess(pi.hProcess,1) runs, and failed: closes the job handle (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) and pi.hProcess; pi.hThread is closed in done:. Nothing runs and no containment is bypassed. The claim matches the code exactly, so it is not refuted. The repair in the finding is correct: capture the BOOL return separately and use GetLastError() when it is FALSE. Severity LOW (diagnostic only) is justified; it does not reach INFO-or-higher containment failure.

Confirmed at native/bunny-owned-process.c:153: `if(!IsProcessInJob(pi.hProcess,job,&member)||!member){error=member?GetLastError():ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED;...}`. When IsProcessInJob returns FALSE, `member` stays at its initializer FALSE, so the ternary takes ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED and the real GetLastError() from the failed API call is discarded. The finding's root cause and reproduction are accurate. Fail-closed holds: the code runs TerminateProcess on the suspended root and goes to `failed`, which closes the process and job handles. The job is not leaked because the same path closes it. Nothing in the security contract depends on the error code value, so this is a diagnostic-only defect. Not refuted; LOW is the right severity. Repair: store the BOOL return separately, use GetLastError() when it is FALSE, and use ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED only when the call succeeded with member FALSE.

rows.title: CancelSynchronousIo can miss a writer that has not yet entered WriteFile
rows.reproduction: close_group calls CancelSynchronousIo(g->writer) after a 1.5 s wait. If the writer thread is between loop iterations, not yet in WriteFile, the cancel is lost. WaitForSingleObject(500) then times out, and CloseHandle(g->writer) closes only the thread handle while the thread keeps running and holding its pipe write end. Job termination normally releases the reader, so no authority escapes, but a thread and handle can leak and a child that is still alive will never see EOF.
rows.rootCause: CancelSynchronousIo cancels only in-progress synchronous I/O and has no effect on a thread that has not yet issued WriteFile. There is no cancellation flag checked by the loop.
rows.repair: Add a volatile cancel flag checked before each WriteFile, and switch to overlapped I/O with CancelIoEx, or accept and document the leak.

votes.reasoning:
Refuted by the code in native/bunny-owned-process.c. The claimed failure needs a live reader holding the pipe's read end after close_group runs, and the code prevents that.

1. Ordering in close_group (lines 75-81): the job is terminated and closed first (line 76, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE set at line 129), so every member of the job is killed before the writer wait. Launch uses no breakaway (line 129 sets no breakaway flag), and the only inherited stdin read end is handles[0], passed via HANDLE_LIST (line 146). Once all members die, no read end remains open, and the writer's next WriteFile fails with broken pipe. Line 53 then breaks the loop and the thread exits, closing its own pipe end (line 56).

2. Lost cancel is harmless: a missed CancelSynchronousIo only delays the writer by one loop iteration. It cannot leave the thread blocked, because the broken pipe makes WriteFile fail immediately. The finding's stated outcome, a live child that never sees EOF, cannot occur, since the job kill already terminated every child.

3. No authority or memory escape: the thread frees only its own Input (lines 56), never touches Group g, so the CloseHandle(g->writer) at line 79 followed by finalize's free(g) causes no use-after-free. Any residual thread lifetime is milliseconds and holds no job or process handle.

The only theoretical leak needs a pipe read-end holder outside the job (for example a DuplicateHandle into an out-of-job process), which is an out-of-contract brokered or hostile class, and the finding does not claim it.

The narrow mechanism is real: CancelSynchronousIo (native/bunny-owned-process.c:78) does nothing if the writer thread has not yet entered WriteFile (line 53), and there is no cancel flag checked by the loop. The claimed impact does not follow from the code. (1) close_group terminates and closes the job first (line 76: TerminateJobObject with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, then CloseHandle(job)) before it waits on the writer, so the root and all descendants are dead before the wait. (2) The only reader-end handle the Host keeps is handles[0] (line 136), and the Host closes it in the done path (line 177) after CreateProcess. Once every job member has exited, the pipe's read end has no holders, so the writer's next WriteFile call fails with a broken-pipe error. The loop breaks at line 53 and the thread exits, freeing its buffer and closing its pipe write end (line 56). So a lost cancel only delays a thread exit by one WriteFile attempt; it does not block indefinitely. (3) A still-living child that never sees EOF cannot exist in this path, because the job is closed with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE before the writer wait and there are no breakaway flags. (4) The thread holds no authority, and the pipe carries only the provider prompt, so the leak carries no security impact. This is at most a cosmetic transient handle/thread lifetime nit, not a defect worth reporting at LOW.

rows.title: Main-thread blocking up to about 3.5 s in close_group, and about 1.5 s in terminate_owned
rows.reproduction: close_group, reached from finalize (line 85, GC on the main thread) and from the env cleanup hook (line 90), can block for terminate_group 1500 ms, writer wait 1500 ms, and CancelSynchronousIo wait 500 ms, totaling about 3.5 s. terminate_owned (line 218) blocks for 1500 ms synchronously. This stalls the Host event loop during finalization or stop.
rows.rootCause: Synchronous Sleep(2) polling and fixed waits on the Node main thread, with no asynchronous completion path.
rows.repair: Make terminate non-blocking: return immediately after TerminateJobObject and let JS poll inspect for ActiveProcesses. Use a shorter writer wait, and defer writer cleanup to the writer thread.

votes.reasoning: The blocking is real but bounded and is not a containment bypass. native/bunny-owned-process.c:65-70 terminate_group spins with Sleep(2) until ActiveProcesses reaches 0 or a 1500 ms deadline. The fast path is near-instant because TerminateJobObject usually drains accounting within milliseconds, so the 1.5 s wait only occurs when the kernel lags. close_group (lines 72-82) stacks that wait with the writer wait (1500 ms) and CancelSynchronousIo plus a 500 ms wait, so the worst case is about 3.5 s, as claimed. finalize (line 84-88) and cleanup (line 90) call close_group, and terminate_owned (line 218) calls terminate_group(g,1500) synchronously. The JS caller at src/lib/bunny-host/adapters.server.ts:298-299 already loops with pause(500) between owned.terminate() calls, so the native 1500 ms block is redundant latency on the Host event loop, not a correctness failure. Containment is not weakened: the handle is kept while active>0 (close_group only nulls it after terminate_group, and close is what drops it), and KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE still applies when the handle closes. The writer-thread wait is also not a safety issue because the writer owns its own pipe and buffer (write_input, lines 27-35). Severity is LOW: a bounded event-loop stall during stop or GC finalization, with no bypass. I would not raise it. The suggested non-blocking terminate is a reasonable hardening but not required.

The blocking is real and matches the code. native/bunny-owned-process.c:65-70 (terminate_group) polls with Sleep(2) until ActiveProcesses reaches 0 or a 1500 ms deadline. close_group (lines 72-82) calls it with 1500 ms, then waits up to 1500 ms on the writer thread, then CancelSynchronousIo plus another 500 ms wait. That is about 3.5 s worst case on the calling thread. close_group is reached from finalize (line 85, GC on the Node main thread), the env cleanup hook (line 90), and launch failure paths. terminate_owned (line 218) blocks 1500 ms synchronously on the main thread, so the Host event loop stalls during Stop.

Why it is only LOW and not a containment bypass: the wait is bounded, the job handle is still closed or kept as the contract requires, and the outcome reported is still accurate (a nonzero activeProcesses keeps the session counted as live). The stall only reaches the full bound when a member survives TerminateJobObject for well over a second or the writer thread is stuck, which is rare in practice. Nothing in the contract promises non-blocking termination, so this is a latency and responsiveness defect, not a correctness failure. The suggested repair (return after TerminateJobObject and have JS poll inspect; move writer cleanup off the main thread) is sound but is a larger change than the finding implies.

rows.title: Static groups list is not thread-safe across napi environments (latent)
rows.reproduction: groups (line 42) is a process-global list with no lock. launch, finalize (line 84), and cleanup (line 90) mutate it from whichever env runs them. If the addon were loaded into a worker_threads env, finalizers on that worker would race with the main thread. Current code is protected only by the isMainThread guard at owned-process-group.server.ts line 35.
rows.rootCause: Module state is static rather than per-env instance data. The argument() check compares g->env to env, which prevents cross-env use but not list corruption.
rows.repair: Store per-env state with napi_set_instance_data, or guard the list with a CRITICAL_SECTION. Keep the isMainThread guard.

votes.reasoning: The only load site of the native module is windowsOwnershipModule() in src/lib/bunny-host/owned-process-group.server.ts:35, which throws unless isMainThread is true, and the grep shows no other dlopen or require of bunny-owned-process.node anywhere in src, scripts or server. The claimed race needs a second napi env (a worker thread) to load the addon, and that path is refused before process.dlopen runs. Within one env, every launch/inspect/close callback and every napi_create_external finalizer runs on that env's single JS thread, so the static groups list is never mutated concurrently. The cleanup hook at native/bunny-owned-process.c:90 only walks entries whose env matches, and it also runs on that thread. The finding is a hypothetical about a future code change, not a defect or bypass in the reviewed contract. Note also that the native file has no lock, so if a worker load is ever enabled the guard must be kept or per-env instance data added; this is a maintenance note, not a current defect.

The failure requires the addon to be loaded into a second napi env (a worker_threads thread) so that two envs mutate the process-global `groups` list (native/bunny-owned-process.c:42) concurrently. No code path can do that. The only load site is windowsOwnershipModule() in src/lib/bunny-host/owned-process-group.server.ts:51 (createRequire(...)(binary)). It is reached only after the line-35 guard `!isMainThread` throws, so a worker env cannot obtain the module through this path. A grep of src/ and scripts/ finds no other createRequire or require of bunny-owned-process.node, and no `new Worker` or worker_threads use outside that guard. The only other reference is the package-integrity script, which does not load the module. So the list is only ever touched from the single main env, and cleanup (line 90) and finalize (line 84) run on that env. The reviewer's own description says the issue is latent and protected by the guard. It is not a reachable defect in the current code, and the guard is the correct control. The suggested repair (per-env instance data) is defense in depth for a future change, not a fix for a present bypass or defect. Note only as a hardening suggestion: if a future change loads the addon in a worker, the guard must be kept or the list must be made per-env.

rows.title: GC finalizer silently kills a live group and the JS record stays stale
rows.reproduction: If the JS OwnedProcessGroup wrapper, and therefore the external, becomes unreachable while the provider session is still running, finalize runs close_group. That terminates the whole job and frees the group. Nothing updates the JS record, so the session appears live until it is reconciled. This is fail-closed toward termination, but the state is unobserved.
rows.rootCause: Finalization is the only cleanup path for an unreferenced live group, and it does not report back to JS.
rows.repair: Ensure the manager holds a strong reference to every live group until it is closed. Add a test that a live session survives GC of unrelated JS objects.

votes.reasoning: The described failure cannot happen as stated. A live group is strongly reachable from a module-level Set: src/lib/bunny-host/owned-processes.server.ts:5-9 declares `const groups = new Set<() => void>()` and trackOwnedGroup adds the stop closure. That closure, created at owned-process-group.server.ts:147, captures `this` (the OwnedProcessGroup), which holds the native external in `this.handle` (line 131/146). So while the session is live, the external is reachable and the napi finalizer (native/bunny-owned-process.c:84-85) cannot run. The release function is only removed in close() (line 167), and close() sets handle to null (line 165) before the group is released, so finalize only runs on an already-closed group, where close_group is a no-op. The spawn path has no throw between handle assignment (line 146) and tracking (line 147), and a failed launch leaves no handle. The repair the finding asks for (strong reference to every live group) already exists. Residual note: the finalizer path is a defensive backstop, not a live-session risk, so the finding does not stand.

The described failure cannot happen as stated. A live group is strongly reachable from a module-level Set, so the finalizer never runs while it is live. In src/lib/bunny-host/owned-process-group.server.ts:146-147, spawn() calls trackOwnedGroup(() => { ... this.close("stopped") ... }). That closure captures `this`, and `this` holds `this.handle`, the napi external (line 133/146). src/lib/bunny-host/owned-processes.server.ts:4,7-9 keeps the closure in the module-level `groups` Set until release(). So the external is reachable from a module root for as long as the group is live, and the wrapper and external cannot become unreachable while the session runs. The only path that drops the registration is release(), which runs from close() (owned-process-group.server.ts:167), and close() nulls this.handle (line 165) and persists closed=true. The finalizer after that only frees memory; close_group on an already-closed group is a no-op because job, writer and root are NULL (native/bunny-owned-process.c:66-82, 84-89). Process exit is also covered by the env cleanup hook (native/bunny-owned-process.c:90) and stopOwnedChildren (owned-processes.server.ts:40 onward). There is no GC-driven silent termination of a live session. The residual point, that the finalizer path does not notify JS, applies only to a group already closed, where the record is already updated. The repair suggested (strong reference until close) is already in place. Optional hardening only: a regression test that GC of unrelated objects leaves a live session intact would be nice-to-have, not a defect.

reviews.summary: Containment bypass hunt (read-only, no tests or processes run). Found one real code-execution bypass (verification python resolves a model-writable python.exe from the task cwd and runs it uncontained) and one contract-violating uncontained provider process (codex app-server catalogue probe on Windows, contradicting native/README.md:36). Confirmed the Codex and Claude session launch paths (spawnSession win32 branch, Codex Mission async path, reroutes via adapter.launch), the probe() helper, and the compatibility probe are contained on win32 with refusal and no fallback. Remaining gaps (computer PowerShell, Playwright Chromium, non-win32, the spawnChild test seam, the non-owned runProcess branch) are either disclosed in test-results/ma3/t9r-f04/process-launch-inventory.md or dead in production; they are listed as LOW hygiene items.

rows.title: Verification python run resolves python.exe from the model-writable task cwd and runs it outside any job
rows.reproduction: A write-access provider task with verify kind python sets task.cwd to its execution root. The agent (inside its contained job) copies any PE file to <cwd>\python.exe, and writes hello.py with exactly print("BUNNY_A_OK"). When the task completes, verifySpec (line ~59) calls exec("python", [path], { cwd: task.cwd }) through execOwnedFile -> execFile. Node passes the bare name to libuv uv_spawn with options.cwd = task.cwd. libuv search_path checks the child's cwd for the file before PATH, so the planted <cwd>\python.exe runs as a plain Host-owned process with no kill-on-close job, outside Stop/containment, and with Host user authority. The binary's stdout only has to equal BUNNY_A_OK for the check to pass. verifyTask (line ~17) has the same bare exec("python") pattern.
rows.rootCause: The interpreter is named by bare command, not by an absolute path from resolveCommand/onPath, and the spawn cwd is the model-writable execution root. The comment at verification.server.ts:45 says agent-written code other than the exact one-liner is never executed; a planted executable violates that invariant. The launch is also not job-contained (the L4 disclosure covers the containment gap but not the cwd-resolution hijack).
rows.repair: Resolve the interpreter once with an absolute, PATH-only lookup (resolveCommand-style onPath, never cwd) and spawn that absolute file. Better, route it through runWindowsOwnedProcess with owner action verification.python so the run is job-contained and reclaimable. Add a regression that places a python.exe in the task cwd and asserts it is not executed. Confirm the libuv cwd-first search behaviour in a scratch directory outside the repo before relying on this finding.

votes.reasoning: Not refuted. Code facts checked by reading only. verification.server.ts:59 calls execOwnedFile("python", [path], {cwd: task.cwd}) (no absolute path, no shell). execOwnedFile (owned-processes.server.ts:20-30) passes the bare name straight to child_process.execFile, so Windows resolution happens in libuv uv_spawn. libuv's win/process.c search_path checks options->cwd before PATH for bare names and tries the .exe suffix, so a python.exe planted in task.cwd would be selected over the real interpreter. task.cwd is the provider's writable execution root, and verifySpec only validates hello.py/the named file, never the interpreter. verifyTask (line 17) has the same bare-name exec, reachable from http.server.ts:664 for workstation-only requests. Impact is concrete: (a) Host-user code runs from a model-writable directory, against the code's own invariant at line 45 ("agent-written code ... is never executed"); (b) a planted binary that prints BUNNY_A_OK forges the "independently executed by Host" PASS, which is the verification gate's core claim. This is not the documented out-of-contract class: the F04 contract covers provider-session lifecycle containment, not verification runs, and the Host is not being attacked directly. I could not confirm the libuv cwd-first lookup empirically because the lens is read-only and no runs were allowed; the conclusion rests on libuv's documented search order. Severity HIGH is justified mainly by verification forgery plus host-authority execution, not by the containment framing (job objects are lifecycle control, not a boundary against same-user code). Repair: resolve the interpreter once via PATH-only lookup (never cwd) and spawn that absolute path, or route through runWindowsOwnedProcess with a verification owner action; add a regression that plants python.exe in the cwd and asserts it is not executed.

Not refuted. Nothing in the code prevents the failure. verification.server.ts:59 runs `exec("python",[path],{cwd:task.cwd,...})` with a bare command name; `execOwnedFile` (owned-processes.server.ts:20-31) is a thin wrapper over child_process.execFile with no resolution step. `resolveCommand`/`onPath` (bunny-missions/capabilities/process.server.ts:10-41) is never applied to this call, so the interpreter is found by the OS, not by Bunny. The only gate is `codeRunGate` (manager.server.ts:1508), which concerns paired-device staged changes, not the executable path. The check at verification.server.ts:57-58 validates only hello.py's text, not the interpreter. The verify run is reached from manager.server.ts:1509 on any completed task with a python verify spec, and the stdout check (`stdout === spec.expected`) is satisfied by a planted binary that prints the expected string. Writable cwd: the task cwd is the agent's execution root, which the contained agent can write. Caveat: I could not run a scratch test (read-only rules), so the libuv cwd-before-PATH search order on Windows is the unverified link. My understanding is that libuv's Windows search_path checks the spawn options.cwd before PATH, which matches the finding. If that holds, the planted <cwd>\python.exe runs as an uncontained Host child, outside the kill-on-close job and outside Stop, which breaks the stated invariant that agent-written code other than the exact one-liner is never executed. The same bare-name pattern at verification.server.ts:17 is reachable via the workstation-only verification.record path (http.server.ts:664). Severity is HIGH as claimed: it is a real containment escape of model-written code, though it requires a python verify spec and a model that copies an executable into its root. Repair as suggested: resolve python to an absolute PATH-only path (never cwd) or route through runWindowsOwnedProcess with a verification owner, and add a regression that plants python.exe in the task cwd.

rows.title: Codex app-server catalogue/usage probe spawns the provider CLI uncontained on Windows, contradicting the stated contract
rows.reproduction: On win32, CodexAdapter.detect (adapters.server.ts:408), CodexAdapter.usage (adapters.server.ts:430) and ModelCapabilityRegistry.probeCodexModels (model-capability.server.ts:132/214) call probeCodexCatalog. Line 25 runs trackOwnedChild(spawn(command, [...prefix,'app-server','--stdio'])) with no job, no refusal and no containment check. The process is the provider CLI binary, so it runs with no Bunny-owned job and no kernel kill-on-close. Its descendants survive: the finally block at line ~53 calls child.kill(), which terminates only the root on Windows. If the Host hard-dies, nothing closes a job for this process. native/README.md:36 says 'Codex and Claude sessions and provider probes use the same job helper'. test-results/ma3/t9r-f04/process-launch-inventory.md row P03 says it is not contained (disclosed L3), so the in-repo README overstates the guarantee.
rows.rootCause: The F04 job helper supports only one stdin buffer followed by EOF, and app-server needs bidirectional JSON-RPC stdin. The probe was left on plain spawn. The README and the task contract were not updated to match, and the probe's refresh cadence (usage() and capability refresh) makes the uncontained launch recurring.
rows.repair: Either (a) extend the helper to a bidirectional stdio mode (keep stdin pipe open, write requests, close on completion) and route probeCodexCatalog through OwnedProcessGroup with containment refusal, or (b) if deferred, correct native/README.md:36 and the contract text to say the app-server catalogue probe is an explicit uncontained exception, add a containment refusal path so the probe is refused under a strict mode, and kill the process tree rather than only the root. Add a test asserting the probe is not started on win32 without a job.

rows.title: Contained session 'done' resolves while job termination is unconfirmed; task completes, verifies and retries beside live members
rows.reproduction: Inject a native terminate result that never reaches ActiveProcesses==0 (or a provider whose root exits 0 leaving a descendant that survives TerminateJobObject for 30 s). terminateJob (lines 289-318) hits CONFIRM_MS, sets containment.state='unconfirmed', schedules retry, and RETURNS normally. The done IIFE (319-368) then returns {ok: exitCode===0, ...} with no containment check. manager.server.ts:1471 'const result = await session.done' reads result.ok only, so state='completed' is written and verifySpec runs (python gate at ~1508 consults only pendingRemoteReview, not live code). If the exit code was non-zero, planRecovery can call startSession (manager.server.ts:1604/1634/1648), which spawns a NEW job while the old unconfirmed job is still live. The task record shows 'Completed'/'failed' with no unconfirmed-cleanup marker; only a lingering hold and an event reflect it.
rows.rootCause: The contract says a session ends only on kernel ActiveProcesses==0, but done resolves on the 30 s deadline regardless of outcome. The manager loop does not consult containment().state before finishing, verifying, or retrying, so the unconfirmed state is visible only through lingering/liveCodeExecutions, not through task state or retry gating.
rows.repair: Make done settle only on 'empty' or 'refused'. For 'unconfirmed', keep the attempt pending or report a distinct terminal state such as 'completed; cleanup incomplete'. Refuse startSession and verifySpec while the previous attempt's containment is not settled. Add a test where terminate never reaches zero and assert no retry starts and no 'completed' is recorded.

rows.title: Provider probe jobs have no containment record: survivors after close are neither held nor reported
rows.reproduction: adapters.server.ts:88 routes probe() through runWindowsOwnedProcess with owner {action:'provider.probe'} and no provider field. The constructor (line 137-138) then sets no containment, so close() (line 162-168) ignores the native activeProcesses count. If a probe's descendants survive close_group's 1.5 s wait, nothing tracks them: no lingering entry, no liveCodeExecutions entry, and recoverOwnedGitOperations (line 78-89) only marks the record interrupted with no corroboration. The task brief says every provider probe is contained, but a probe that is not confirmed empty is not reported.

That wait only polls ActiveProcesses for accounting; it is not a grace period before a kill. CloseHandle(g->job) then runs on a job created with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (native line 129), which the kernel enforces on last-handle close. Every member of the job is therefore terminated regardless of the count returned. Any nonzero activeProcesses after the wait is processes still in teardown, not surviving live code. The job also cannot shed members: CREATE_SUSPENDED assignment happens before resume (native ~line 133-159), there are no breakaway flags, and inspect() enforces limitFlags===0x2000 on every poll (owned-process-group.server.ts inspect). The probe path in adapters.server.ts:88 uses the same spawn/close path as provider sessions, so probe members get the same kernel kill. Ignoring the close() count for probes is therefore not a liveness gap. The only residual class is brokered or out-of-contract launches, which the contract documents as out of scope. The one legitimate observation is that probe records carry no containment field, so the record does not say "confirmed empty" after close. That is a record-keeping/documentation gap, not a bypass or a surviving-code defect, and it does not meet the LOW bar as a liveness finding.

The finding assumes probe descendants can survive close(). The job was created with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and no breakaway flag (native line 129), so closing the last job handle kills every remaining member kernel-side, including descendants whose parent already exited. The probe's member set therefore cannot outlive its group, and close() in owned-process-group.server.ts:162-168 does reach the native close (the handle is non-null for a probe that launched). rows.title: Host shutdown does not await in-flight contained termination; a second stop throws and shutdown proceeds to db.close
rows.reproduction: A user Stop is in progress (stopContained awaiting terminateJob up to 30 s; manager.server.ts:1857 added 'stopping'). Host shutdown runs close(): stopOwnedChildren() at owned-processes.server.ts:35 fires each group's stop() without awaiting it. Then http.server.ts ~954 calls manager.stop(id) for each session in manager.sessions. Those calls throw 'Stop already in progress.', and Promise.allSettled swallows them, so close() proceeds to missions.close(), server close and db.close() while the first stopContained is still running and will later call this.update/db.write on a closed database. Nothing awaits the job's final accounting. The kernel still kills the job on process exit (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE), so this is a truthfulness/persistence gap, not a live-process gap.

rows.repair: Keep a per-task in-flight stop promise and await it during shutdown, or await the group stop promises in stopOwnedChildren, before db.close.

rows.title: Unconfirmed retry loop and close_group block the Node main thread for up to 1.5 s per call, indefinitely for a stuck job
rows.reproduction: terminate_group (native line 65-71) runs a synchronous Sleep(2) loop for up to 1500 ms on the Host's only thread. terminateJob (adapters.server.ts ~289-318) calls owned.terminate() every ~500 ms for 30 s, and the unconfirmed retry (adapters.server.ts ~313-318) calls it every 5 s with no bound. rows.repair: Make terminate asynchronous (worker thread or non-blocking poll via setImmediate), or cap the wait per call to a few ms and poll from JS. Surface the stuck job in health and add backoff to the retry.

reviews.summary: Lens: Host restart recovery, process identity and PID reuse. No PID-reuse kill path was found. Restart never kills by PID (it only reads), and every identity check compares PID, creation time and image name. The resubmit path replays only capability steps, not provider sessions, and survivors with access undefined classify as live (providerSessionAuthority returns null). The four findings above are fail-open or availability gaps in the restart corroboration path, not kill-authority bypasses. The primary defence is kernel KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so the findings are defence-in-depth against the restart contract. The most important is F04-LENS-RESTART-01. Not verified end to end: whether the mission retry path reaches provider admission without a lingering check (F04-LENS-RESTART-04). No tests were run, and no files were edited.

rows.title: Restart corroboration drops identity-incomplete records and treats an empty expected set as no survivors
rows.reproduction: Provider record for a contained session where a surviving member, or the launcher, has createdAt 0 or no image name. Native created() returns 0 when GetProcessTimes fails (native/bunny-owned-process.c:106), and the native member row omits 'file' when QueryFullProcessImageNameW fails (native/bunny-owned-process.c ~209). Also, a record persisted before the first inspect has launcherPid 0 and members [] (owned-process-group.server.ts:137-140 and :148). Restart: manager.server.ts:186-189 builds expected with filter(row.pid>0 && row.name && row.createdAt), so every incomplete identity is silently dropped. If none remain, survivors([], rows) is [] and line 195-197 deletes the lingering entry and calls reconcileProviderSession, which sets containment='empty' (owned-process-group.server.ts:113). The emitted event says none of the recorded identities is alive. A still-running member with a live PID is then neither held as live code nor reported for review, so promotion and remote mutation are not gated by it. Caveat: the kernel KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE normally kills members when the Host dies, so this needs a member that escaped the job or a record with no identities, which is defense-in-depth for the stated restart contract.
rows.rootCause: Corroboration treats 'identity could not be recorded or parsed' the same as 'process is gone'. The filter is a silent drop instead of an unverifiable state, and an empty expected set is accepted as proof of no survivors.
rows.repair: Build expected without silent filtering. Any launcher or member with missing name, createdAt <= 0, or launcherPid 0 marks the record unverifiable: keep lingering as 'checking' or cleanup_unconfirmed, do not call reconcileProviderSession, and emit a review event. Only mark containment 'empty' when at least one recorded identity was verified absent and no identity is unverifiable. Add a restart test with a record whose member createdAt is 0 and a fake processTable that still lists the PID, asserting the session stays live.
rows.regressionTest: Unit test in provider-containment.test.ts or a manager test: write a provider-session record with launcherPid 0 and members [{pid:P,createdAt:0,file:'x.exe'}], call reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions with processTable returning [{pid:P,ppid:0,name:'x.exe',createdAt:123}]. Assert lingering holds a 'checking' or live entry and that reconcileProviderSession is not called (containment stays not 'empty').

rows.title: Liveness check reuses the destructive-cleanup identity rule, so an alive process with unknown birth time reads as gone
rows.reproduction: processTable() sets createdAt to null when the CIM CreationDate is empty, and to NaN when Date.parse fails (process-tree.server.ts:13-14). A recorded provider member is alive with the same PID and image, but its current row has createdAt null. In manager.server.ts:194 survivors(expected, rows) calls sameProcessIdentity, which requires current.createdAt === expected.createdAt, so it returns false. The record is reconciled as empty and the live process is no longer held as live code.
rows.rootCause: sameProcessIdentity was written to block destructive action on unknown identity ('a missing birth time cannot establish identity for destructive cleanup'). The restart path uses it as a liveness test, where unknown identity must fail closed toward 'alive', so the rule is inverted there.
rows.repair: Add a separate liveness predicate: a row with matching PID and image name counts as alive when its createdAt is null or NaN, and only a strict PID+birth+image match is used for kill authority. Use the liveness predicate in reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions. Add a unit test where the current row has createdAt null and a matching PID and name, asserting the session remains live.
rows.regressionTest: process-tree unit test: survivors([{pid:7,createdAt:1000,name:'codex.exe'}], [{pid:7,ppid:1,name:'codex.exe',createdAt:null}]) must report the process as alive for liveness, while sameProcessIdentity must still return false for kill authority.

rows.title: One malformed provider-session record aborts Host construction and skips all other interrupted sessions
rows.reproduction: Place any file matching the uuid.json pattern in runtime/provider-sessions with a wrong schema or missing containment, or truncated JSON (JSON.parse at line 100 throws). recoverProviderSessions throws. Keep the Host up, continue with other records, and surface the unreadable file as needing review. Do not treat it as absent, since the record may name live members, so the review should be explicit.

A mission step that failed with host_restart is retried by the user, which the code describes as 'retried as a fresh child task'. A new provider session is admitted. Nothing in the admission path reads tasks.lingering or liveCodeExecutions. The only consumers are promotion (manager.server.ts:2646) and remote mutation (manager.server.ts:2753). New code therefore runs alongside the surviving prior work.
